title: Orphaned VNI teardown causing cross-tenant DNS mapping and intermittent isolation breaches
creator: Marco Chen
description: Production incidents reported by multiple Dedicated customers where tenant A's DNS responses were intermittently resolved by tenant B after tenant A scaled down. Symptoms: stale hostnames, cross-tenant response correlation, and transient connection failures for outbound requests. Investigation indicates a race during VNI/overlay teardown that leaves stale L2/L3 mappings on a subset of edge nodes, combined with a DNS cache/response multiplexing behavior on our egress proxies.
root_cause: When a tenant's GPU pool scales down we initiate VNI teardown on the overlay. Due to a timing window, some edge nodes received the teardown but others retained per-tenant L2 learning entries and stale SNAT bindings. Our egress resolver uses multiplexed UDP sockets and a shared cache keyed loosely by host name; stale L2/L3 bindings caused responses to be routed via a node that still had the old tenant context, which then returned DNS answers or proxied TCP connections associated with the previous tenant. The main contributing factors: (1) non-atomic VNI drain order, (2) delayed cleanup of L2/L3 state on dataplane nodes, and (3) insufficiently partitioned DNS response cache on egress proxies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two dedicated tenants (T1 and T2) in the same region sharing overlay segment.
2) Drive outbound DNS-heavy traffic from T1 (long-lived flows) to warm resolvers and create SNAT allocations.
3) Scale T1 GPU pool to zero rapidly while T2 remains active.
4) Observe intermittent DNS mappings returned to T2 clients that reference T1 hostnames, or see connection attempts routed to T1-backed endpoints.
5) Reproduce rate increases by toggling scale-down timing and adding synthetic DNS cache churn.
Note: reproducible on canary with forced teardown timing and overlay instrumentation enabled.
mitigation: Short-term mitigation rolled out within 3 hours: (a) introduce an aggressive L2/L3 state invalidation hook on teardown events for all dataplane nodes, (b) disable DNS response multiplexing on egress proxies for dedicated tenants while we stabilize, (c) added a temporary conservative SNAT eviction policy to avoid immediate reuse across tenants. These actions reduced customer-visible errors by >90%.
fix: Code: make VNI teardown transactional — ensure teardown signals are acked by all dataplane nodes before marking tenant offline (refactor overlay controller).
Control plane: add explicit per-tenant L2/L3 reconciliation loop with idempotent cleanup and backoff-aware retries.
Egress: partition DNS response caches and per-tenant UDP socket namespaces to prevent cross-tenant responses.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs to canary environment and enable transactional teardown for 10% of tenants (canary group includes low-risk internal tenants).
2) Monitor canary for 48 hours focusing on DNS mismatch alerts and SNAT reuse counters.
3) Gradually increase to 50% then 100% over 72 hours if no regressions.
4) Re-enable controlled DNS multiplexing only after per-tenant cache partitioning verified.
5) Run post-deploy reconciliation job to clear any leftover L2/L3 entries across the fleet.
Rollback: revert overlay controller to previous behavior and re-enable DNS multiplexing.
monitoring: Alert: TENANT_DNS_MISMATCH (severity P0) — fires when resolver returns hostname mapping not matching tenant id on node
